defects.canonical: The loop bound `range(1, len(lines) - 1)` stops at the second-to-last element, so when `text` has no trailing newline the final data row is never yielded. Should be `range(1, len(lines))`.
defects.why_subtle: The `- 1` reads as defensive guarding against a trailing empty line, and inputs that happen to end in a newline mask the loss, so review and naive tests both pass.

defects.canonical: _split_fields splits each line on every comma, so a quoted field containing a comma (e.g. "Smith, Jr") is broken into two cells and every later column shifts. The parser does not honor CSV quoting.
defects.why_subtle: split-on-comma reads as a deliberate simplification; its effect (silent column misalignment) only appears on data that actually contains a quoted comma.

defects.canonical: dict(zip(header, cells)) stops at the shorter of the two, so a row with MORE fields than the header silently drops the extra trailing cells with no error. The docstring covers ragged short rows but not over-long ones.
defects.why_subtle: zip truncating to the shorter iterable is idiomatic and looks intentional; the data loss only happens on malformed over-long rows and never raises.
